review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped for uses of its declarations across the project. I did not run Lean. The one finding is the pair-decomposition iff, which callers always apply with explicit `rw`. The other lemmas have hypotheses or non-trivial side conditions (a function graph, subset, nesting), so they are poor simp candidates. The one uncertainty is whether a plain `@[simp]` could interact with other pair-membership simp lemmas in downstream files. I could not check that without running Lean.

findings.excerpt:
theorem flatLimitConditionCode_pair (stages history levels row A : ZFSet.{u}) :
    FlatLimitConditionCode stages history levels (ZFSet.pair row A) ↔
      FlatHistoryCuts stages history levels row A := by
findings.problem: This is the canonical constructor-style decomposition of the opaque predicate `FlatLimitConditionCode` on a pair. It has no hypotheses and its right side is strictly simpler: the existential and equation are gone. It is not marked `@[simp]`. Every downstream user instead applies it by hand with `rw [..., flatLimitConditionCode_pair]` or `(flatLimitConditionCode_pair _ _ _ _ _).1`. These sites are GroundFlatLimitConditions.pair_mem_flatLimitConditions, GroundFlatLimitAdequacy, GroundRecursiveRefinementBinaryUnions and GroundForcingHistoryLimitConnection. The def is also not reducible, so simp cannot normalise `FlatLimitConditionCode … (pair row A)` to `FlatHistoryCuts …` by itself. The rewrite terminates, because the target mentions no `FlatLimitConditionCode`, and it cannot loop.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the lemma `@[simp]`. The orientation is already correct, from the pair-code predicate to `FlatHistoryCuts`. Then `rw [M.mem_flatLimitConditions, M.pair_mem_stageOneCandidateBound, flatLimitConditionCode_pair]` and similar call sites can become `simp [M.pair_mem_stageOneCandidateBound]`. If the project wants a restricted simp set instead, add a dedicated simp lemma for `pair ∈ flatLimitConditions` using `pair_mem_flatLimitConditions`.
findings.benefit: Callers get the normal form `FlatHistoryCuts stages history levels row A` automatically. This removes repeated manual rewrites and makes membership goals such as `pair row A ∈ flatLimitConditions …` reduce by simp.
